hero.headline: The brain starts forming opinions
hero.sub: A thesis is a claim your project makes about itself — falsifiable, with its predictions written down before the evidence arrives. The brain stops only remembering what happened and starts holding a position on what is true.

shot.alt: A validated thesis open: the claim, 88% confidence with a supporting/contradicting/no-signal breakdown, three ticked pre-registered predictions, and a dated evidence ledger citing the task and changelog entries behind them
shot.caption: 88%, three predictions that held, and every entry in the ledger naming where it came from.

blocks.title: How a thesis earns its confidence

items.title: The claim is falsifiable
items.text: "Hybrid recall beats BM25F on the gold set by enough margin to ship it on by default" can be wrong. "Recall feels better" cannot, so it isn't a thesis.

items.title: Predictions come first
items.text: You register what you expect to see BEFORE looking — precision at least 5 points higher, zero regressions, no threshold changes. Each one ends up supported, contradicted, or still open.

items.title: Evidence is a cited ledger
items.text: Every entry names its source — a changelog line, a task, a run — and carries a verdict: supports, contradicts, or no-signal. A no-signal entry counts as work done and nothing learned.

items.title: Confidence is arithmetic
items.text: It is derived from the ledger, not felt. When it crosses the line, the thesis flips to validated or invalidated with a prediction check written into the record.

blocks.title: Re-tested while you sleep
blocks.body: Theses move across a board — draft, open, validated, invalidated — and open ones are re-tested every sleep cycle against whatever evidence arrived since the last one. A position you took in June has to keep surviving July, and the cycle that flips one also records which predictions held.

shot.alt: The Hypotheses board with Draft, Open, Validated and Invalidated columns, a summary strip counting each state, and a stamp reading when the last learning cycle checked them

blocks.title: Funnels in Lab, not in a spreadsheet
blocks.body: Insights gained a funnel view: an all-funnels comparison table, a per-funnel step lane with drop badges, click any two steps for their A→B conversion, plus filters, breakdowns and compare. On long funnels, every step whose change isn't significant can fold away, so what's left on screen is what moved.

shot.alt: A funnel's step lane: session start through sign-up, onboarding, paywall view and trial start, each step showing its share of the top and the drop to the next, with a metrics panel alongside
shot.caption: Every step carries its own drop — the −69% into Trial start is where this funnel actually breaks.

blocks.title: And release notes moved into the app
blocks.body: What's New shipped in this version: a page in the sidebar, a once-only popup on the launch after something lands, and unread tracked per release rather than by a watermark. This page you are reading is that feature.

shot.alt: A release opened in the full-screen reader, showing its version, headline, cover screenshot and the newer/older pager

blocks.text: Theses are opt-in — `dreamcontext theses enable`. Left off, the sleep cycle behaves exactly as it did before, and the Hypotheses page stays out of your way.

closer.title: Try it on something you argue about
closer.body: Write down the claim you keep re-litigating and the two or three things you'd expect to see if it were true. From then on every sleep cycle checks it for you.
